item.title: The uncomfortable truth about money
item.description:
Money is essential for modern life. We spend our lives earning it, saving it and worrying about it. But we also tend to think it makes us selfish, corrupt and less connected to one another. What if money has actually made us more moral?
Host Megan McArdle talks with economist Cameron Harwick about how money has made societies more virtuous, not less. They discuss how markets changed the way we cooperate with strangers, why religion and community still matter in a money economy and what society’s discomfort with money reveals about today’s political fights.
